name: Brazil

glass.bottle.mass_g: ASSUMPTION on the shape; the upper bound was widened from 750 g on 13 Nov 2026 to include the 950 g of the 1 L returnable soft drink bottle in Brazil (Morini, Hotza and Ribeiro 2019, masses from the manufacturer)
pet.recycling_rate: SOURCE: 56.4% of post consumer PET packaging recycled in Brazil in 2021 and just over 56% in 2024, 410 kt (ABIPET, Censo da Reciclagem do PET no Brasil, 2022 and 2025 editions)
hdpe.recycling_rate: SOURCE: 23.1% of plastic packaging recycled in Brazil in 2020 (Picplast, cited by CEMPRE, Recycling Rates in Brazil); all plastics together
ldpe.recycling_rate: SOURCE: 23.1% of plastic packaging recycled in Brazil in 2020 (Picplast, cited by CEMPRE, Recycling Rates in Brazil); all plastics together
aluminium.recycling_rate: SOURCE: aluminium beverage cans recycled in Brazil: 100% in 2022, 98.7% in 2021 (ABRALATAS and Recicla Latas, cited by CEMPRE); collected mostly by waste pickers
pet.incineration_share: SOURCE: municipal waste in Brazil in 2023: 58.5% to sanitary landfills, 41.5% to dumps and controlled landfills, under 0.2% to refuse derived fuel (ABREMA, Panorama dos Resíduos Sólidos no Brasil 2024); no incineration, dumps are modelled with the landfill dataset

glass.end_of_life.source: SOURCE: 25.1% of glass packaging recycled in Brazil in 2024 (Circula Vidro audit, reported by the Paraná state government, 2025), 25.8% in 2018 (Abividro, cited by CEMPRE); the rest goes to landfills and dumps, there is no incineration (ABREMA, Panorama 2024)
